components.text: Perfect goodness supplies a reliable expectation of benevolent, life-directed creative intention.
Whether perfect divine goodness makes a life-permitting world materially more expected than it is under naturalism.
Whether apparent purposive signs can establish intentional agency more securely than benevolent character.
Single-universe naturalism makes life-permitting observations extremely improbable relative to theism.
The likelihood comparison must use the aggregate probability of admissible naturalistic explanations rather than one austere rival.
Whether the naturalistic likelihood denominator must aggregate multiple admissible alternatives rather than use one austere hypothesis.
Tailored naturalistic alternatives must be admitted and aggregated whenever they can accommodate the observation.
Naturalistic agency alternatives can persistently weaken empirical identification of a benevolent divine source.
Whether unrestricted tailoring of naturalistic alternatives illegitimately neutralizes every possible item of empirical theistic evidence.
Whether deceptive-agent possibilities specifically weaken inferences from purposive signs to benevolent character.
The stalking-horse method implausibly eliminates every possible empirical comparison between theism and naturalism.
A consequential likelihood claim must specify theism and outperform the full admissible naturalistic family.
Whether the legitimate evidential demand is comparative performance across specified theistic and naturalistic hypotheses, not absolute empirical decisiveness.
Whether the original likelihood comparison covers every admissible naturalistic version and a sufficiently specified theistic hypothesis.
The pro side must specify its theistic hypothesis and the complete naturalistic comparison class.
The comparison must encompass the admissible naturalistic alternatives rather than one selected hypothesis.
Whether the pro thesis specifies both its theistic hypothesis and the full class of naturalistic hypotheses it claims to outperform.
Whether aliens, simulations, and similar alternatives fall inside the stated single-universe naturalistic comparison class.
Empirical evidence can meaningfully discriminate theism from broad naturalistic agency alternatives.
Classical perfect-being theism has enough predictive content to outperform naturalistic alternatives.
Whether empirical events can favor general theism when the intentions of both divine and naturalistic agents remain unspecified.
Whether specifying broad worldview classes supplies sufficiently determinate likelihoods for particular intentional events.
General theism and general alienism predict a particular resurrection equally poorly because both leave agent intentions unknown.
Evidence of intentional agency does not securely identify benevolent purposes.
Whether perfect divine goodness supplies a non-arbitrary likelihood bridge to revelation and resurrection that generic alien agency lacks.
Whether benevolent character can provide predictive content beyond bare intentional agency.
The probabilities of tailored naturalistic alternatives must be aggregated against theism.
The pro case must compare specified theism with the complete admissible naturalistic family.
Theistic agency is too unconstrained to enjoy a meaningful likelihood or prior advantage.
Whether the full comparison should weight specific augmented-naturalistic rivals by their conditional share within general naturalism.
Whether aggregating life-directed alternatives gives them substantial prior probability within the broader naturalistic family.
Whether perfect-being theism has a sufficiently large conditional share within general design possibilities.
It is implausible that broad naturalistic alternatives prevent every possible empirical adjudication between theism and naturalism.
Religious context and divine goodness generate an empirical likelihood advantage over generic naturalistic agents.
A sufficiently specified theism can empirically outperform all single-universe naturalistic alternatives.
Whether broad rival compatibility removes comparative evidential support rather than merely preventing logically decisive proof.
Whether simulation and science-fiction hypotheses fall within a sufficiently broad naturalistic class to remain empirically compatible.
Simulation possibilities can accommodate nearly any observation and thereby sustain empirical underdetermination.
Simulation belongs in the aggregated naturalistic alternative space that may neutralize theism's advantage.
Whether simulation hypotheses genuinely explain fine-tuning or merely transfer the same explanatory demand to base reality.
Whether simulation deserves material weight within the aggregated naturalistic rival family.
Perfect-being theism receives a larger conditional prior than any tailored naturalistic specification because it is simpler.
Classical unlimited theism has an intrinsic advantage over the broad comparison class.
Whether an unlimited perfect-being hypothesis retains a simplicity advantage after all specifically limited alternatives are aggregated.
The aggregate prior of all specifically limited alternatives massively exceeds that of a single unlimited hypothesis.
Breadth and modesty of the rival family are sufficient to establish its comparative advantage.
Whether the modesty gained by aggregating limited alternatives necessarily outweighs the unlimited hypothesis's claimed coherence.
Coherence may give perfect-being theism an intrinsic-probability advantage over modest disjunctions.
Theism is intrinsically simpler and therefore receives a larger conditional prior.
Whether ontological parsimony supplies an independent naturalistic prior advantage even if modesty or coherence favors theism.
Whether theism's claimed simplicity within design offsets its additional supernatural ontology.
Life-permitting parameter values are an objective, highly improbable datum requiring comparative explanation.
Whether apparent fine-tuning is an objective universe-level datum rather than evidence that the operative physical theory is defective.
Perfect divine goodness supplies a defensible expectation that God would create life-permitting conditions.
Perfect goodness supplies predictive content concerning revelation and valuable conscious life.
Perfect-being theism is sufficiently specified to receive determinate comparative likelihoods and priors.
Whether perfect goodness yields a sufficiently determinate expectation that God would choose a life-permitting universe.
Whether calling God good fixes particular values, reasons, and intended actions such as creation or revelation.
